headline: High: shared MCP and filesystem-capable agent pair creates prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python interfaces, while nullclaw can use MCP plus read/write filesystem and browser/web tools. That creates a direct instruction-ingestion path where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be parsed by the other as trusted guidance. The shared MCP bridge makes prompt injection plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is forwarded into nullclaw's MCP or file inputs without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF nullclaw writes instructions into a shared workspace that MemMachine later reads, the content can steer MemMachine.
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the agents.
Require provenance labels on all inter-agent messages.
Route shared content through a sanitizer that strips instructions.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add allowlisted message schemas for agent-to-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and secrets such as API keys and private keys. Nullclaw also has broad network egress, so if shared files or context are exposed across the pair, sensitive data can leave the local boundary. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or memory namespace, sensitive data can cross from one to the other.
IF nullclaw forwards shared context to external APIs, leaked data can exit the environment.
mitigations: Separate storage for each agent.
Restrict nullclaw egress to approved endpoints.
Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on files and memory.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; MemMachine can use MCP and APIs that may also touch shared resources. Because both agents can participate in the same workspace or integration layer, overlapping write paths can race or overwrite each other. The profile evidence is enough to treat this as a dangerous default conflict rather than a read-only overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF nullclaw modifies git state while MemMachine writes via an MCP-backed workflow, state corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable git mutation in one agent.
Use read-only mounts for MemMachine.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is a conversational agent that can emit context-rich outputs, and nullclaw has scheduling, webhook, browser, and shell capabilities that can act on those outputs. If nullclaw treats MemMachine's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or persisted state changes. The pair therefore has a strong default pathway from generated text to downstream action.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes MemMachine output without verification, incorrect facts can be operationalized.
IF MemMachine produces malformed instructions that nullclaw schedules or executes, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before actions.
Add schema validation on MemMachine outputs.
Use confidence thresholds before execution.
Log and diff all proposed actions.
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution roles.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is documented as handling long-term user facts and conversational context, while nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and webhook payloads. That combination creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and sensitive-data handling, even though no specific residency or certification conflict is documented. Because the profiles are docs-only and the exact policy gap is unclear, medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both agents with different retention rules, compliance drift occurs.
IF webhook payloads or workspace files contain regulated personal data, retention and deletion obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data classes.
Align retention settings across both agents.
Exclude secrets from logs.
Document deletion/export procedures.
requires-engineering: map each data class to a policy owner.
